alignments.note: Participle rendered by the bare English participle.
Preposition realized by *unto* (rule 36).

The article precedes and governs the head noun ἀρχηγόν across the interposed genitive τῆς πίστεως, so it takes the English *the* under rules 19 and 57; the ASV's word order places *the author* after *Jesus*.
Bare noun; the marginal *captain* is an alternative rendering only.
Coordinating conjunction.
Bare noun.

No genitive pronoun or other source word is present to take the supplied *our*, so rule 20's second arm applies and the article realizes the possessive, with the case preposition *of* riding along as in rule 21; rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics from making *our* `added`.
Bare noun, its determiner slot taken by the article's *our*.
Name, fronted in the ASV's word order; rule 15 permits the reordering.
Relative pronoun.
Preposition realized by *for*; the ASV writes no *sake* frame here, so rule 78 is not in question.
The article precedes the noun χαρᾶς it governs, so under rule 31 it is that noun's determiner and takes *the*; the relativizer goes to the participle, which is what carries the finite clause.

Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause: *that* and *was* are rule 31 helpers on the participle, and *before* belongs to πρόκειμαι's own English gloss *set before*. Head on the lexical *set* under rules 9 and 17.
Dative pronoun realized by *him*.
Bare noun, its determiner already on the article.
Finite verb.
The Greek is anarthrous, so no article competes and the supplied *the* is an ordinary rule 51 helper on the noun it determines.
Participle rendered by the bare English participle.
Genitive object of καταφρονήσας, rendered by the bare noun.
Connective particle realized by *and*.
Perfect indicative with its auxiliary; *down* is part of καθίζω's English gloss *sit down*. Head on the lexical *sat* under rules 9 and 17.
Preposition realized by *at*.

Substantival adjective with anarthrous Greek: it is the nominal word, so it takes the supplied determiner itself under rule 58, and *hand* is the generic completion. Rule 17's generic-noun clause keeps the head on *right*.
Article carrying the case preposition: *of the* is one unit headed on *the* under rule 21, and the noun stands alone.
Bare noun.
The ASV gives θεοῦ no determiner, so this article has no English *the* to anchor and is `unrepresented` under rules 21 and 23; the case preposition stays with the noun.
Determinerless English phrase, so rule 21 keeps the bare *of* with the noun rather than on the article.

review_notes: s004 τῆς → *of our*: taken under rule 20's second arm, since no genitive pronoun stands to take the supplied *our*. Reading *our* as `added` under rule 11 was rejected because the ASV's italics are evidence rather than a verdict.
s003 governs ἀρχηγόν across the interposed τῆς πίστεως (rule 57), not the following genitive; the form-ambiguous accusative confirms it.
s013's *before* is kept inside the participle's unit as part of πρόκειμαι's own gloss *set before*, not read as a separate preposition.
